title: The Best Southern Fried Chicken
description: Crispy, flavorful and absolutely divine! A crunchy exterior with moist, juicy chicken on the inside.
author: Brandie Skibinski
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut up (or 8 pieces of your favorite cuts of chicken)
instructions: Place cut up chicken in a large bowl. Sprinkle salt, garlic powder, and onion powder on top and toss to coat.
Add buttermilk and hot sauce, stir until combined. Cover with plastic wrap and let marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, salt, paprika, and black pepper. Set aside.
Fill up a deep fryer with peanut oil and preheat to 325°F (300°F if using a cast iron skillet).
Take chicken pieces one at a time, let the excess buttermilk drip off. Coat in the flour mixture and shake off excess. Let sit for a few minutes.
Carefully add chicken pieces to the deep fryer, frying until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F. Dark meat takes about 12-14 minutes, white meat 8-10 minutes.
Place fried chicken on a paper towel-lined tray and sprinkle flaked salt on top. Serve.
notes: Let the chicken soak for a minimum of 2 hours; overnight for best results.
Cornstarch helps give an extra crunchy exterior; omit if undesired.
Use peanut oil for the best frying experience, but canola or vegetable oils work as well.
An electric deep fryer helps maintain proper temperature, especially for frying novices.

title: Easy Classic Shrimp and Grits
description: Cheesy, creamy stone-ground grits topped with buttery shrimp and crumbled bacon. Southern comfort food in 30 minutes.
author: Elizabeth Lindemann
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups chicken broth, preferably low sodium, divided
1 lb. jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined
Thinly sliced green onions, for garnish (optional)
instructions: Bring 2 cups of the chicken broth, the milk, 3 tablespoons of the butter, and a pinch of salt to a gentle boil in a medium-sized pot. Add the grits and whisk together. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until grits are soft and creamy, whisking every few minutes. Cover and set aside off heat.
Cook the 4 bacon strips until crispy in a nonstick or cast iron skillet. Set aside on a paper towel-lined plate. Once cool, chop into small pieces.
Drain all but 2 tablespoons of the bacon grease from the skillet.
Rinse the shrimp with cold water and pat dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cook in the bacon grease until only just cooked, about 2 minutes per side.
Add the remaining tablespoon of butter and 1/2 cup of chicken broth to the shrimp and stir until melted and broth is heated. Taste and add salt if necessary.
Stir the cheese into the grits until melted. Taste and add salt if necessary.
Serve the shrimp mixture over the grits, spooning some of the liquid from the skillet over the grits, and sprinkle with the bacon pieces and sliced green onions, if using. Serve immediately.
notes: Best served right away, since shrimp get rubbery when reheated and grits firm up as they cool.
You can use water instead of chicken broth to cook the grits.
Quick-cooking grits save time, but the texture will be different from stone-ground.
Yellow or white grits both work.

title: Cajun Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
description: A rich, comforting dark roux, tender chicken, smoky andouille sausage, and classic Cajun seasoning.
author: Mike Hultquist
ingredients: 1 pound chicken thighs, chopped (chicken breast is good, too)
Salt and pepper to taste (about 1 teaspoon each)
12 ounces andouille, sliced into 1/4 inch slices
1/2 cup peanut oil or vegetable oil
2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, or more to taste
4 tablespoons chopped parsley, plus more for serving
1 tablespoon filé powder, or to taste (optional)
instructions: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven to medium heat. Add 1 teaspoon oil and heat until it shimmers.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper, then add it to the pan along with the sliced andouille. Cook a couple of minutes per side until the sausage is browned at the edges and the chicken is lightly golden. Set aside.
Deglaze (optional): pour in 1/4 cup chicken broth and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot, then pour this liquid over the reserved meat.

Add 1/2 cup peanut oil to the pot and heat to medium. Add the flour and stir. Cook for 20-30 minutes, stirring constantly, until the roux turns the color of chocolate and smells toasty and nutty (not burnt).
Add the peppers, onion, celery, and garlic. Stir and cook for about 5 minutes, until the vegetables soften.
Add chicken and andouille. Stir and cook for 1 minute to coat everything in the roux.
Add the okra, Cajun seasoning, and chicken stock. Stir and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add the bay leaves, partially cover, and cook at medium-low heat for at least 1 hour to thicken, stirring occasionally. Simmer 2-3 hours for a richer flavor. Taste and adjust for salt.
Stir in parsley and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve in bowls over white rice and garnish with extra parsley. Serve filé powder on the side so everyone can sprinkle some in.
notes: The roux is the key to a great gumbo. It darkens from blond to copper to deep chocolate brown, and each stage adds a different layer of flavor.
Okra is traditional and helps thicken, but it's not required.
Traditional Cajun gumbo usually doesn't include tomatoes, but it's your pot.
Cajun and Creole food isn't meant to be HOT, but it is boldly seasoned.

title: Authentic Cajun Red Beans and Rice
description: Creamy, velvety New Orleans red beans made with bacon, smoked ham, and smoky andouille sausage, served over white rice.
author: Lauren LeBlanc
ingredients: 1 pound andouille or smoked sausage, sliced
1 cup diced green bell pepper (1 large)
1/2 cup thinly sliced green onion, divided
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley, divided
Long grain white rice, for serving
instructions: Soak: The night before, sort through the beans and remove any stones. Cover with cold water by a few inches and soak overnight. Drain and rinse before cooking.

Sear: Heat a large pot over medium heat. Cook the bacon until mostly crispy, 10-15 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon, leaving some grease in the pot. Sear the sausage until browned on both sides, 5-10 minutes (in batches if needed). Set aside with the bacon.

Sauté: Add onions, celery, and bell pepper and cook, stirring, until the onions are translucent and starting to caramelize, 8-10 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Simmer: Return the bacon and sausage to the pot with the beans, chicken stock, ham, oregano, thyme, black pepper, half the parsley, half the green onions, and the bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook uncovered about 2 hours, until beans are tender and the liquid has reduced. Skim any foam and stir occasionally.
Smash: For thicker beans, smash some against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon.
Season: Stir in the remaining green onions and parsley. Taste and add Cajun seasoning, salt, or pepper as needed.
Serve: Remove and discard the bay leaves. Serve over rice topped with green onions and parsley, with hot sauce on the side.
notes: Don't salt until the end — the bacon and sausage add plenty. If the beans end up too salty, simmer a quartered potato in the pot to absorb some salt.
A smoked ham hock can stand in for the diced ham.
Soak beans at least 12 and up to 24 hours.
Leftovers keep 3-4 days in the fridge (store separately from rice) and freeze well for up to 6 months.
Red beans get better with time — feel free to make them a day ahead.

title: Old-Fashioned Chicken and Dumplings
description: The real deal, the way a Southern great-grandmother made it: flat strips of dough simmered in a savory broth with tender chicken.
author: Brandie Skibinski
ingredients: 2-3 chicken breasts (about 3 cups of cooked chicken)
All-purpose flour, for rolling out the dumplings
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
Place the chicken breasts on the baking sheet, drizzle with the oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Bake for about 45 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F. Shred it with two forks.
Pour the chicken broth into a large pot and start warming it on the stovetop while you make the dumplings.
In a medium bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Add the cold cubed butter.
Work the butter in with your fingers, a fork, or a pastry cutter until it resembles tiny pebbles.
Pour in the milk and mix it all together.
Dust your counter generously with flour. Place the dough on the counter and dust it with more flour.
Roll the dough out to about 1/4" thickness, adding more flour as needed to keep it from sticking.
Use a knife or pizza cutter to cut the dough into squares.
Dust the dumplings with a bit more flour — it keeps them from sticking and helps thicken the broth.
Bring the broth to a boil. Add the shredded chicken and stir.
Add the dumplings one at a time so they don't stick together, stirring frequently.
Cook the dumplings 15-20 minutes. The broth will thicken and the dumplings may sink a little as they soak up the broth.
Taste one — it shouldn't taste doughy. Then serve!
notes: This version traditionally has no vegetables, but you can add peas and carrots if you like.

title: Southern Baked Macaroni and Cheese
description: Classic soul food custard-style mac and cheese with eggs, evaporated milk and plenty of cheese — creamy, browned on top, and heavenly.
author: Kelly Wildenhaus
ingredients: 1/2 cup (1 stick) butter, cut into small pieces
1/2 pound Velveeta, cut into small chunks
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil. Cook the macaroni just shy of package directions (al dente). Drain well and place in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
In the same pot, whisk together the whole milk, evaporated milk, eggs, salt, pepper, and sugar. Pour over the macaroni.
Add the butter, sour cream, Velveeta, Colby-Jack, and sharp cheddar. Stir to combine well and top evenly with the mild cheddar.
Bake 35-40 minutes until bubbly and lightly browned on top. Let rest about 10 minutes before serving.
notes: People swear by Velveeta in this recipe — don't substitute it.
Grating your own cheese melts better than pre-shredded.
It will be a little oily on top after baking; blot with a paper towel while it rests if you like.
Reheats great in the microwave. Fantastic alongside collard greens and fried chicken.

title: Southern Collard Greens with Smoked Turkey
description: Soulful collard greens simmered in chicken broth with onions, garlic, and a smoked turkey leg. A must at any Southern holiday table.
author: Monique Kilgore
ingredients: 1 fully cooked smoked turkey leg (or smoked turkey wings)
Seasoning (optional: salt, pepper, vinegar, hot sauce)
instructions: Remove the collard green leaves from the stems.
Wash the collards several times in cold water to remove any dirt and grit.
Rinse well and set aside.
In a large pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the onions and garlic until tender.
Add the chicken broth, red pepper flakes, and turkey leg. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20-30 minutes.
Add the collard greens. Simmer, covered, 45-60 minutes or until your desired tenderness.
Season to your preference and serve.
notes: For best flavor, make sure your broth is well-seasoned before adding the greens.
You can raise the heat if needed, but don't boil the collards.

title: Southern Fried Green Tomatoes
description: Pan-fried green tomatoes with a crispy, golden cornmeal coating — tender and juicy on the inside.
author: Jazzmine Woodard
ingredients: 1 quart grapeseed oil or frying oil of your choice
instructions: Prep: Line one sheet pan with parchment and another with paper towels. Slice the tomatoes about 1/4 inch thick, discarding the ends. Pat each slice dry.
Set up three shallow dishes: flour in one; eggs whisked with buttermilk in another; cornmeal mixed with all the seasonings in the third.
Batter: Dip each tomato slice in the flour, then the egg mixture, then the cornmeal mixture. Lay on the parchment-lined pan to rest.
Heat the oil: Fill a cast iron skillet with about 2 inches of oil and heat over medium-high to 350-375°F. A pinch of cornmeal should sizzle when dropped in.
Fry: Cook 4-6 slices at a time until golden brown, 3-5 minutes, without crowding the pan. Flip and cook until the other side is golden, then drain on the paper towel-lined pan.
notes: Best eaten fresh. You can prep the dredging station up to two days ahead to make frying quicker.
Pat both sides of each tomato slice dry to remove excess moisture.

title: Southern Cornbread (Buttermilk & Cast Iron)
description: Stone-ground cornmeal, tangy buttermilk, no sugar, and a crunchy crust from a screaming-hot cast iron skillet.
author: Sharon Rigsby
ingredients: 1/4 cup peanut oil, plus 1 tablespoon to grease the skillet
instructions: Preheat your oven to 450°F.
Add 1 tablespoon of oil to a 10-inch cast iron skillet and heat it in the oven for 5-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk together the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a smaller bowl, mix the eggs, buttermilk, and peanut oil.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry just until moistened. A few lumps are fine — don't overmix.
Carefully remove the hot skillet and swirl the oil to coat the bottom and halfway up the sides. Pour in the batter.
Bake about 20 minutes, until golden brown, pulling away from the sides, and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the skillet on a rack for 5 minutes.
Invert onto a plate, or cut into wedges and serve straight from the skillet.
Serve piping hot with plenty of butter.
notes: Don't skip preheating the skillet — adding batter to a hot pan is what makes the crust crispy.
No buttermilk? Stir 2 tablespoons lemon juice or white vinegar into just under 2 cups whole milk and let it sit 5 minutes.
Great for Thanksgiving dressing. Cooled and tightly wrapped, it freezes for up to 30 days.
Store cornmeal in the refrigerator or freezer.

title: Southern Biscuits
description: Simple, from-scratch butter biscuits — a Southern breakfast favorite and perfect for biscuits and gravy.
author: Paula Deen
ingredients: 3/4 cup milk (more or less as needed)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Cut the butter into the mixture until it looks like cornmeal.
Make a well in the flour mixture and slowly add the milk into the middle. Knead the dough with your fingers, adding milk as needed.
Roll the dough out on a lightly floured surface to your desired thickness. Cut with a small biscuit cutter.
Butter the bottom of a skillet and place the biscuits in the pan. Bake 12 minutes or until golden brown.
notes: Space the biscuits apart so they don't touch while baking for crunchier edges all the way around.
Reviewers love swapping the milk for buttermilk.

title: Old Fashioned Peach Cobbler
description: Easy from-scratch peach cobbler made with fresh or canned peaches, so you can enjoy it all year round.
author: Lauren Allen
ingredients: 5 peaches, peeled, cored and sliced (about 4 cups)
instructions: Add the sliced peaches, sugar and salt to a saucepan and stir to combine.
Cook on medium heat for a few minutes, until the sugar dissolves and the peaches release their juices. Remove from heat and set aside.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Slice the butter into pieces and add to a 9x13-inch baking dish. Place the pan in the oven while it preheats to melt the butter, then remove.
In a large bowl mix together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Stir in the milk just until combined. Pour over the melted butter and smooth into an even layer.
Spoon the peaches and juice over the batter. Sprinkle cinnamon generously over the top.
Bake at 350°F for about 38-40 minutes. Serve warm, with a scoop of ice cream if desired.
notes: To use canned peaches, substitute 1 quart jar, undrained.
Gluten-free: use gluten-free flour.

title: Pecan Pie
description: The best easy old-fashioned pecan pie, with a rich caramel pecan filling and a flaky, buttery crust.
author: Lauren Allen
ingredients: 1/3 cup salted butter, softened or melted
instructions: Place the pie dough in a deep dish pie plate and refrigerate while you prepare the filling.
In a large bowl, cream together the sugar, brown sugar, salt, corn syrup, and butter. Mix in the eggs and vanilla.
Reserve a few pecans and stir the rest into the filling. Pour into the unbaked pie shell and arrange the reserved pecans on top, spooning a little filling over them.
Bake at 425°F for 10 minutes, then lower to 350°F and bake about 50 minutes more. Check halfway and tent with greased foil. It's done when the center isn't overly jiggly when gently shaken.
Cool completely for several hours before cutting, or refrigerate 1-3 days until ready to serve.
notes: Can be made 1-3 days in advance and stored in the refrigerator.
To freeze, cool completely, wrap in plastic and foil, and freeze up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge.

title: Southern Banana Pudding
description: An heirloom recipe: rich homemade custard layered with vanilla wafers and fresh bananas, topped with an airy meringue.
author: Robyn Stone
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Combine the flour, sugar and salt in a large, heavy saucepan.
Lightly beat the egg yolks and combine with the milk. Pour into the dry ingredients in the saucepan.
Cook over low to medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and smooth. Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla.
Layer 1/3 of the vanilla wafers in a 2-quart oven-safe glass bowl.
Place 1/3 of the sliced bananas on top of the wafers.
Pour one-third of the custard over the wafers and bananas.
Repeat the layers two more times, ending with a final layer of wafers.
Whip the egg whites with an electric mixer at high speed.
Once foamy, add the cream of tartar, then gradually add the sugar one tablespoon at a time until stiff peaks form. Stir in the vanilla.
Spread the meringue over the pudding, making sure it reaches the edges of the dish.
Bake about 25 minutes, until the meringue is lightly browned.
notes: Keeps covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
No-bake version: skip the meringue and top with whipped cream.

title: Southern Sweet Potato Pie
description: An heirloom recipe loved for generations — baked sweet potatoes, butter, milk, eggs and sugar. Perfect for Thanksgiving.
author: Robyn Stone
instructions: Bake the sweet potatoes: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Scrub the potatoes, prick each 4-5 times with a fork, and bake on a baking sheet 45-50 minutes until tender. Cool and peel.
Make the filling: Mash the sweet potatoes with the butter until smooth. Add the sugar, vanilla, milk, and eggs and mix until well combined. Pour into the unbaked pie crust.
Bake the pie until the center is set, about 1 hour. Cool slightly before serving.
notes: For a brown sugar version, swap the granulated sugar for 3/4 cup brown sugar.
Store covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, or freeze up to 3 months.
